newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Congress board approves Canada trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Chile Congress board approves Canada trade pact.

text.p: A special Chilean Congress commission approved Tuesday a free trade agreement signed last year between Chile and Canada.
The treaty was passed by the eight deputies on the board from the ruling center-left coalition, while deputies from the rightist opposition parties either abstained or rejected the pact.
The accord must now be approved by the deputies' finance commission before being voted on by the chamber before May 21.
Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said he was satisfied with the vote backing the pact which may come into force in July.
"(The agreement) will have a favorable impact on employment, on the improvement in salaries in the medium term as well as on trade and investment," he said.

Chile and Canada agreed a bilateral accord after talks on Chile's bid to join the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) stalled over a year ago as the result of internal political difficulties in Washington.
Chile was invited to join NAFTA, which links the United States, Canada and Mexico, at the Summit of the Americas in Miami in December 1994.
